one_liner: Graceful Kansai "flower of the turf" whose poise hides a relentless inner tsukkomi comedian.
personality: Outwardly she is elegant, patient and dignified, always "standing straight under the sun" and enduring like the lilac that blooms after winter. Inside (her parenthesised inner-voice lines) she is a loud Kansai comedian who can't stop retorting, gets spooked by stains and wood patterns, and agonises over radio-show submissions and ego-searching. With her trainer she plays the straight man (tsukkomi) to their gags and openly enjoys it, calling them her best comedy partner.

story_arc.summary: Her titles trace a flower budding, wilting and reblooming: she wins early (Hanshin JF), runs the Triple Tiara (Oka Sho, Oaks, Shuka Sho), stalls as a "bud" again, and returns through the Nakayama Kinen, Osaka Hai and Victoria Mile to reclaim a crown at the Queen Elizabeth II Cup ("The crown revived") before the Japan Cup. Arcs like "Beside the Queen" and "Even though the sky looked high" set her as the one chasing a dazzling star (Almond Eye) while enduring like a lilac through winter. The wiki notes she trains alongside Almond Eye and plays straight man to a gag-prone trainer.

sample_lines.en: The lilac is a flower that endures the winter to bloom. ...I am the same. I'll bloom all the more vividly for what I endured.
